name: Query

hero.title: TanStack Query, minus the re-render.
hero.lede: The same query core you trust for caching, dedup and refetching, with every result field as its own signal. When data changes, one text node updates: 1 derivation where `@tanstack/react-query` does 8.

facts.value: `@tanstack/query-core` 5<small>Re-exported, so `QueryClient` and friends import from here.</small>
5.6× faster than react-query<small>Same core, happy-dom, one run.</small>
WebSocket, SSE, streams<small>`useSubscription`, `useSSE`, `useStream` write into the same cache.</small>
{dot:warn}`useQuery` on iOS and Android<small>Experimental; lowers to a native `PyreonQuery`.</small>

why.title: What changes when the cache is made of signals.

items.title: One field changes, one node updates
items.text: `data`, `error`, `status`, `isFetching` and the rest are separate signals, created only when you first read them. A background refetch flips `isFetching` without touching the text that shows the name.

items.title: Keys that read signals
items.text: Options are a function, so `queryKey: ['user', props.userId]` tracks the prop. Change it and the query refetches. No dependency array to forget.

items.title: Live data, same cache
items.text: `useSubscription` (WebSocket, reconnect with backoff), `useSSE` and `useStream` hand you the `QueryClient`, so a push message can patch or invalidate cached data the rest of the app already reads.

items.title: Declare a query once
items.text: `queryOptions`, `infiniteQueryOptions` and `mutationOptions` give one typed definition for hooks, prefetching and `client.getQueryData` with no generic.

difference.title: Delete the three states and the race.

before.label: React, fetching by hand
before.caption: Three pieces of state, an effect, no cache, and a slow answer for the previous id can overwrite the current one.

after.label: with @pyreon/query
after.caption: Cached, deduplicated, retried, and refetched when `userId` changes. Only the `<h1>` text updates.

demo.title: Three readers, one query.
demo.text: Three boxes read three fields of one query. The counters show how often each one re-ran. Refetch, change the data, or return identical data: each box moves only when its own field does.

features.title: The TanStack surface, plus live data.

items.name: `defineQueries`
items.text: named parallel queries in one declaration.

items.name: `invalidates` on mutations
items.text: `useMutation({ mutationFn, invalidates: [['posts']] })` refetches on success without an `onSuccess`.

items.name: Typed reusable options
items.text: `queryOptions`, `infiniteQueryOptions`, `mutationOptions`; the key carries the data type.

items.name: SSR hydration
items.text: `dehydrate` on the server, `HydrationBoundary` on the client, no refetch on load.

items.name: Realtime
items.text: `useSubscription` for WebSocket, `useSSE` for Server-Sent Events, `useStream` for SSE or NDJSON as reactive state.

items.name: Offline
items.text: `@pyreon/query/persist` restores the cache before the first fetch.

items.name: Native mutations and infinite lists
items.text: `useMutation` over an `@pyreon/http` endpoint and `useInfiniteQuery` lower to iOS and Android. Experimental.

api.title: The hooks, the boundaries, and the core.

limits.title: Pass `useQuery` a function
limits.text: `useQuery(() => ({ … }))`, so the key can read signals and props. `useMutation` takes a plain object.

limits.title: Don't return early on `isPending()`
limits.text: A component runs once, so `if (user.isPending()) return …` pins it to the first branch. Use `<Show>`, `<Switch>`/`<Match>` or an accessor.

limits.title: Create the `QueryClient` once
limits.text: At module scope or app setup, not inside a component that might mount twice.

limits.title: Native covers the common hooks
limits.text: On iOS and Android `useQuery` and `useStream` lower today, and `useMutation` and `useInfiniteQuery` join them in the next release; `QueryClient` config, devtools and suspense queries stay web.

comingFrom.title: Same options, as a function. Same client.
comingFrom.note: Keys, `queryFn`, `staleTime`, `QueryClient` and `invalidateQueries` are TanStack's own. The changes: options are a function, results are called (`user.data()`), branches use `<Match>` instead of early returns, and `invalidates` replaces the `onSuccess` boilerplate.

recipes.title: One query definition, used everywhere
recipes.text: Declare it once; use it in a hook, prefetch it on hover, and read or patch the cache with full types.

recipes.title: Orders that update from a WebSocket
recipes.text: The socket patches the cached list; every component already reading `['orders']` updates in place.

faq.q: Is this a fork of TanStack Query?
faq.a: No. It depends on `@tanstack/query-core` and re-exports it. Caching, retries, dedup and invalidation are TanStack's code; the adapter turns results into signals.

faq.q: The benchmark says happy-dom. Does that matter?
faq.a: Yes: happy-dom is a JavaScript DOM, so the ratio and the derivation counts mean something and the absolute times do not. It is one overnight run that we wrote. Reproduce with `bun run --filter=@pyreon/query bench:react-query`.

faq.q: Where is react-query just as good?
faq.a: Across components. If one component reads only `status` and another only `data`, react-query's tracked props skip the right one too; that row is a tie in the docs. The gap is inside a single component that reads several fields.

faq.q: Can I use the TanStack devtools?
faq.a: Yes: `<QueryDevtools />` from `@pyreon/query/devtools` is the TanStack panel.
